ety.text: Derived from Proto-Slavic *korkъ (“limb”) with the suffixes -атый (-atyj, “-provided”) and -ица (-ica, “feminine suffix”), thus roughly meaning the legged one. The form корока́тица (korokática) would thus be the etymologically correct one, but the most used one is карака́тица (karakática), influenced by кара- (kara-, “(from Turkish) black”).

From Proto-Turkic *kïŕïl (“red”). Thoroughly replaced the native Slavic word (дёрен (djóren) from *dernъ) early as also with Belarusian кізі́л (kizíl), while Ukrainian дере́н (derén) is still more common than кизи́л (kyzýl). Compare Ottoman Turkish قزلجق and Turkish kızılcık (cornelian cherry).
